summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening dyspnea on exertion and epigastric pain. Initial evaluation revealed no myocardial infarction, but a stress test showed borderline ischemic changes, prompting a cardiac catheterization. This confirmed three-vessel coronary disease with significant stenosis in the right coronary artery, leading to percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty and placement of a drug-eluting stent. His symptoms improved post-procedure. The epigastric pain was determined to be related to GERD, worsened by isosorbide mononitrate, which was subsequently reduced. Medications were optimized, including starting diltiazem and adjusting antiplatelet and antihypertensive therapy. The patient was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged.
